affected_kpis: Staffing Level; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Percentage of scheduled clinical staff that become unavailable due to illness, leave, or other unplanned absences beyond normal levels.
prototype_assumption: Staff reduction is applied uniformly across all departments and shift categories. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Does not differentiate by staff seniority, department criticality, or skill mix. A 15% reduction in consultants has a different operational impact than 15% in junior nurses.

affected_kpis: Staff Absenteeism Rate; Staffing Level; Average Patient Waiting Time
business_description: Additional percentage-point increase in baseline absenteeism rate above the hospital's normal monthly average.
prototype_assumption: The increase is additive to the baseline absenteeism rate observed in the synthetic dataset. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Assumes absenteeism increase is uniform across all staff categories. Does not model cascading effects where one absence triggers additional coverage gaps or overtime fatigue.

affected_kpis: Bed Occupancy Rate; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate
business_description: Percentage increase in patient volume above baseline, reflecting seasonal surges, public health events, or referral spikes.
prototype_assumption: Demand increase is proportional across all service areas. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Does not differentiate by patient acuity or service area capacity. A 15% increase in emergency admissions has a different impact than 15% in outpatient volumes.

affected_kpis: Staffing Level; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Number of temporary or locum clinical staff deployed to offset staffing shortfalls and restore service capacity.
prototype_assumption: Each temporary staff member contributes one full equivalent to the staffing level numerator. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Assumes immediate availability and full productivity of temporary staff. Does not account for onboarding time, reduced efficiency, or unfamiliarity with hospital protocols.

affected_kpis: Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Extra operating hours added per day to spread patient load and reduce peak-time congestion.
prototype_assumption: Extended hours reduce waiting time proportionally by increasing total service capacity. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Assumes patient arrivals can be redistributed evenly across extended hours. In practice, demand patterns may remain concentrated during traditional peak periods.

affected_kpis: Staffing Level; Staff Absenteeism Rate; Bed Occupancy Rate; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Number of consecutive days the staffing pressure scenario is simulated, affecting cumulative impact on all headline KPIs.
prototype_assumption: Effects are linear over the scenario duration with no compounding fatigue or adaptation. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Does not model non-linear dynamics such as staff burnout over extended periods, cumulative complaint escalation, or adaptive capacity improvements that may emerge after the first week.

parameter_name: Temporary staffing cost per staff per day
business_description: Daily cost per temporary clinical staff member used to estimate total mitigation expenditure during the scenario.
prototype_assumption: Cost is uniform across all temporary staff categories and does not vary with shift type or seniority. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Real-world temporary staffing costs vary significantly by specialty, shift premium, and agency rates. This single rate is a simplification for scenario comparison only.

affected_kpis: Bed Occupancy Rate; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Percentage reduction in usable bed capacity due to infrastructure issues, maintenance closures, or infection control measures.
prototype_assumption: Capacity reduction is applied uniformly across all wards. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Does not differentiate by ward type or patient dependency. Closing 20% of ICU beds has a fundamentally different impact than closing 20% of general medical beds.

affected_kpis: Bed Occupancy Rate; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate
business_description: Percentage increase in patient volume above baseline, compounding the effect of reduced physical capacity.
prototype_assumption: Demand increase is proportional across all service areas and occurs concurrently with capacity reduction. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Does not model demand elasticity or patient self-triage behaviour. In reality, some patients may defer care or seek alternatives when capacity is visibly constrained.

affected_kpis: Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Number of daily service hours lost due to facility closures, equipment failure, or utility disruptions.
prototype_assumption: Lost hours reduce effective service capacity proportionally. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Assumes lost hours are evenly distributed across the day. Concentrated losses during peak periods would have a more severe impact than the same total spread across low-demand periods.

affected_kpis: Bed Occupancy Rate; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Percentage of lost capacity recovered through temporary measures such as mobile units, ward reconfiguration, or accelerated maintenance completion.
prototype_assumption: Restored capacity is immediately available and meets the same quality and safety standards as permanent capacity. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Temporary capacity may have lower patient acceptance, reduced amenity standards, or higher operational overhead that are not captured in the percentage metric.

parameter_name: Patients redirected to alternative service areas
affected_kpis: Bed Occupancy Rate; Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate
business_description: Percentage of patients diverted to alternative service areas, partner hospitals, or outpatient pathways to relieve pressure on the disrupted facility.
prototype_assumption: Redirected patients are successfully accommodated elsewhere without creating secondary bottlenecks. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Does not account for patient or family resistance to redirection, transport logistics, or capacity constraints at receiving facilities. Assumes seamless transfer.

affected_kpis: Average Patient Waiting Time; Patient Complaint Rate; Patient Satisfaction Score
business_description: Extra operating hours added per day to compensate for reduced capacity and maintain patient throughput.
prototype_assumption: Extended hours restore effective throughput proportionally to the hours added. Thresholds are illustrative prototype values calibrated to the synthetic dataset and are not validated hospital standards.
limitation: Assumes sufficient staffing exists to support extended hours. If staffing is already constrained, extending hours may exacerbate fatigue without improving throughput.

limitation: Does not model adaptive responses such as elective surgery deferral, inter-hospital transfers, or gradual restoration of normal operations over time.

parameter_name: Temporary capacity restoration cost per day

limitation: Real-world restoration costs vary by intervention type (mobile units, accelerated repairs, leased equipment). This single rate is a simplification for scenario comparison only.
